Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services is in discussions with US private equity firm Advent International for a sizeable fund infusion, people familiar with the matter told Moneycontrol.

The proposed investment could give Advent a minority stake in the Noida-based hospital chain, with the deal likely to involve a primary issuance of shares in two tranches, one of the people said.

“The plan is for Advent International to invest up to Rs 3,000 crore in Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services. It’s likely that the proposed deal will have two legs, and the proceeds may come in two tranches, via a primary issuance of shares,” the person said.

However, no final decision has been taken on the quantum of funds or the deal structure, and the discussions may or may not fructify into an eventual transaction, the person added.

A second person said that if the proposed transaction goes through, Advent International could end up with a minority stake of between 20 percent and 24 percent in Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services.

Two other people familiar with the ongoing discussions said that, if talks proceed, the proceeds from the proposed fund raise could be used by the hospital chain for expansion through the inorganic route.

The four people cited above spoke to Moneycontrol on condition of anonymity.

An email query to Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services and its senior management was unanswered at the time of publishing. Multiple reminders had been sent earlier, while attempts to reach company executives by phone were unsuccessful. Advent International also did not respond to an email seeking comment. This article will be updated if and when the companies respond.

The board of directors of Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services is scheduled to meet on September 17 to “discuss and consider the growth plans of the company” through a fund raise, “by way of raising debt, rights issue, preferential allotment or qualified institutions placement”, according to an exchange disclosure.

Advent International, led by Shweta Jalan, has previously invested in the domestic hospital sector through Care Hospitals. It exited the company in 2016 by selling its stake to UAE-based Abraaj Group.

In 2023, Advent re-entered the healthcare segment by investing in Apollo HealthCo, a subsidiary of Apollo Hospitals, giving the PE firm a stake in Apollo’s digital healthcare platform.

Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services had a market capitalisation of Rs 9,474.52 crore at the end of trading on September 15. The promoter category owns a 55.80 percent stake, according to the latest exchange filings.

The company operates eight hospitals across North India, including facilities in Noida, Greater Noida, Noida Extension, Greater Faridabad, Model Town in New Delhi, Faridabad, Jhansi-Orchha in Madhya Pradesh and its recently added hospital in Agra.

Yatharth has also acquired its ninth hospital in Gurugram, taking the group’s total capacity to more than 2,800 beds, according to its LinkedIn page.

According to the firm’s FY26 annual report, “Yatharth is one of North India’s leading private healthcare networks, operating a portfolio of large multi-speciality hospitals focused on tertiary, quaternary and critical care services. Since our establishment in 2008, we have built a strong presence across key micro-markets in the National Capital Region while extending our footprint to the Jhansi-Orchha region.” Ashwin Mohan is Editor (Deals) at Moneycontrol and leads the M&A, private equity and equity capital market transactions coverage.
